title: Malaria incidence per 1,000 population
national_indicator_description: This indicator measures the number of new malaria cases arising in a given year per 1,000 population.
computation_definitions: The incidence of malaria refers to the number of new cases of malaria per 1,000 population per year. In Rwanda, malaria cases are confirmed by microscopic examination or RDT.
computation_calculations: (Number of new malaria cases / Total population ) * 1,000
other_info: Estimates of malaria incidence are produced through a consultative and analytical process led by WHO and are published annually.
comments_limitations: More information on malaria is available in the Rwanda Biomedical Center's annual [Malaria and Neglected Tropical Diseases Reports](https://rbc.gov.rw/publications/reports).
target_name: By 2030, end the epidemics of AIDS, tuberculosis, malaria and neglected tropical diseases and combat hepatitis, water-borne diseases and other communicable diseases
indicator_definition: Incidence of malaria is defined as the number of new cases of malaria per 1,000 people at risk each year.
